collins.hedgehog: None. Collins's comparison company treated its leadership in cigarettes as secure and, instead of deepening brand-building, poured tobacco cash into unrelated diversification (food, container shipping, oil). It lost the No. 1 position to Philip Morris.
hedgehog_key_points: diversified away from what it could be best at
should have doubled down on cigarette brand building
collins.stop_doing: Stop diversifying into unrelated businesses (shipping containers, oil, assorted foods) and stop assuming leadership in cigarettes is permanent; concentrate on brand building against Philip Morris.
stop_doing_key_points: stop unrelated diversification (Sea-Land shipping, Aminoil oil, foods)
stop treating No. 1 position as secure
collins.leader_type: Not Level 5. Collins contrasts RJR's diversification-driven leadership with Philip Morris's focus; the later CEO F. Ross Johnson, who led the 1988 LBO fight in which management stood to gain enormously, is a counter-example to Level 5.
brutal_facts: the Surgeon General's report threatens the core business
Philip Morris's Marlboro is gaining momentum
the company's own researcher had flagged the cancer link a decade earlier
a past brand launch failed expensively

later_history: Formed R.J. Reynolds Foods (1966, Chun King) and bought Sea-Land container shipping (1969), Aminoil (1970, $600M), Del Monte (1979), Heublein (early 1980s) and Nabisco (1985, $4.9B), becoming RJR Nabisco. Marlboro passed Winston in 1976 and Philip Morris passed Reynolds as the U.S. sales leader by 1983. KKR's $24.88B leveraged buyout (1988-89), then the largest ever, saddled the company with debt. Joe Camel campaign (1987-1997) drew charges of marketing to children. Joined the 1998 Master Settlement Agreement. Tobacco split from Nabisco in 1999; merged with Brown & Williamson to form Reynolds American (2004); bought Lorillard (2015); acquired by British American Tobacco (2017).
notes: Direct comparison company for A15 (Philip Morris). Dossier date matched to Philip Morris's 1964 transition (late January 1964, after the Surgeon General's report).
